title: Add scheduler regression test suite for release branches (mixed lengths, backpressure, overload)
author: Leila Farouk
description:
Context: We’ve had a handful of scheduler regressions that only show up under “release branch” constraints (less churn, different knobs, tighter change control) but still need fast signal for backpressure + overload behavior. This PR adds a focused regression test suite for the runtime scheduler that is intended to run as a gating job on release/* and runtime-*-lts branches.

What’s in this PR: 1) New scheduler regression harness that runs deterministically in CI (time is simulated; no wall-clock sleeps) and asserts on queueing, fairness, and load-shedding outcomes; 2) Three core scenarios encoded as tests: (a) Mixed prompt lengths: interleave short (<=256) and long (>=4k) prefill requests and assert no starvation, bounded tail latency in simulated ticks, and correct per-tenant fairness; (b) Backpressure: saturate the prefill stage and assert correct propagation (429/overloaded errors) rather than unbounded queue growth; (c) Overload + recovery: induce overload, verify shed policy triggers at the right thresholds, then recover and verify steady-state returns without “sticky” throttling.

Why now: This is a prerequisite for Runtime LTS. Backports to release branches are higher risk in scheduling, and we need a fast, stable signal that catches the common failure modes without requiring full perf-canary runs.

Design notes: - The harness uses the existing SchedulerSim hooks and adds a thin adapter so we can feed a deterministic arrival trace and capture per-step metrics (queue depth, admitted reqs, rejected reqs, per-tenant service share). - Assertions are on invariants and relative bounds (e.g., starvation window in ticks) rather than absolute latencies. - Tests are tagged @release-branch and run in a dedicated CI job for release/* and runtime-*-lts branches; they also run on main as non-required to keep drift low.

CI / gating: - Adds a GitHub Actions workflow job `scheduler-regression-smoke` that is required on release/* and runtime-*-lts. - Runtime main: runs but is allowed-to-fail for now (we can flip once we’ve burned in for a couple weeks).

Follow-ups: - Add a “burst + jitter” arrival trace variant once we have the LTS perf gate thresholds finalized (separate PR). - Consider adding a minimal GPU-path integration test once runner capacity stabilizes (not part of this PR).

Testing: `bazel test //runtime/scheduler/tests:release_branch_regressions` and CI job `scheduler-regression-smoke`.

Risk: Low to medium. Touches test harness + CI only; no production scheduler behavior changes.

Refs: ENG-4831, Runtime LTS release branch gating work (ENG-4824).
commits: runtime/scheduler/tests: add deterministic regression harness and trace runner
runtime/scheduler/tests: add mixed prompt length fairness regression
ci: add scheduler-regression-smoke workflow for release branches
docs: document release-branch test tag and how to run locally
conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): The mixed-length test is exactly the failure mode we saw last quarter. Request: please avoid hard-coding queue depth numbers; can you assert on monotonic bounds / invariants instead? Also add a note on what “starvation window” means in simulated ticks.

Leila Farouk (author): Updated assertions to rely on invariants (no tenant goes >N ticks without admission while backlog exists) and changed queue depth checks to “does not exceed max_queue * 1.05” with explicit rationale. Added docstring explaining starvation window and how ticks map to scheduler loop iterations.

Connor O'Brien (review): For LTS gating, we need the workflow to run on runtime-*-lts and release/* branches. Can we also ensure it doesn’t require secrets so it can run in fork PRs? And can you make the job name stable for branch protection rules?

Leila Farouk (author): Workflow now uses only read-only permissions and no secrets. Job name set to `scheduler-regression-smoke` (stable). Triggers updated to include `release/**` and `runtime-*-lts` branch patterns. Added a short note in docs/ci/release-branch-gates.md.
Sahana Iyer (review): Bazel cache is missing; job time is ~18 min on cold runners. Can we add remote cache config (read-only) and mark the artifacts to upload the trace summary when it fails?

Leila Farouk (author): Added read-only remote cache (same config we use for other unit suites). On failure, the job uploads `scheduler_trace_summary.json` plus the per-test metrics dump for triage. Runtime stays under 7 minutes on warm cache in my reruns.
Marcus Reed (review): Please add a short section describing how these tests differ from perf-canary and why they won’t catch throughput regressions. I want to avoid over-selling this as a perf gate.

Leila Farouk (author): Added “Scope and limitations” to runtime/scheduler/tests/README.md: these assert correctness invariants under load patterns; perf-canary remains the throughput/latency regression gate. Also added a follow-up TODO for a minimal integration test once runner capacity is available.
Sofia Ivanova (final): Approved. Good balance of deterministic simulation and real scheduler invariants.
Connor O'Brien (final): Approved for release gating. Please coordinate with me when we flip it to required on main after burn-in.
